messages:
Ash: Heads up — starting ~19:02 UTC we saw p95 jump from ~6ms to 120–180ms between gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-17 during the nightly batching window. Heatmap + span traces attached.
ops-bot: alert: cluster-east-1:esw-latency-p95 exceeded threshold (120ms) at 2026-03-17T19:02:14Z :rotating_light:
Lina: which racks are the hot paths? any model fleets pinned to those nodes?
Ash: Mostly rack A2 <-> A3. Affected workloads: rtx-infer-prod (4 replicas), embedding-batch-mux. Fanout looks wider than usual (many connections originated from the same service).
Greg: Any infra changes around that time? ToR or NIC firmware? MTU renegotiation events are my first suspicion.
Maya: We rolled a ToR microcode bump last week (03:00), nothing scheduled tonight. There was a control-plane rollout that touched k8s-proxy at 18:55 but that shouldn't affect E-W NIC paths.
Dave: Quick checklist while we triage:
  1) rdma/tcp counters on both nic endpoints
  2) ethtool stats for dropped frames
  3) tcpdump + rdma pingpong around 19:02
Ash: Running probes now, pasting snippets below.
Ash: ```
$ rdma link show mlx5_0
port 1: state ACTIVE
pkey_violations: 0
rx_packets: 125234
tx_packets: 125198
rx_errors: 0
tx_errors: 12
```
Greg: tx_errors != 0 — could indicate link-layer retransmits or a driver bug. Which kernel/NIC driver are those nodes on?
Ash: Both nodes on 5.15.95 + mlx5_core 5.12.1. Also ran a quick ethtool -S on gpu-node-17:
Ash: ```
TX_DMA_TIMEOUTS: 10
rx_missed: 0
gso_segments: 23456
```
Maya: TX_DMA_TIMEOUTS spikes line up with the p95 window. Sounds like the NIC is having intermittent DMA stalls. Any MTU mismatches along the path?
Lina: can you check ip link on both endpoints and the ToR reported MTU?
Ash: endpoint mtu: 9216 on both nodes. Doing a traceroute to the ToR management IP shows egress MTU 1500 on one interface (suspicious). Traceroute: 3 hops, hop2 (ToR-e3) shows MSS 1460.
Greg: If ToR egress is 1500 while endpoints are 9216, fragmentation/gso offload interplay could cause bursts of stalls under highfanout/batching. We've seen GRO/GSO expose NIC DMA path issues before.
Dave: short test: disable GRO/GSO on gpu-node-17 and re-run the heavy batch for 1 min.
Ash: Running commands now:
Ash: ```
# disable offloads
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
# quick rdma ping (test)
ib_write_bw -d mlx5_0 -s 4096 -t 5
```
Ash: ib_write_bw returned stable ~9.2ms p95 after disabling offloads, previously was ~140ms. Applying change across rack A3 now.
Maya: Nice — that points to offload interaction with ToR path. Still need vendor follow-up for TX_DMA_TIMEOUTS (driver/firmware).
Lina: add to incident timeline: mitigation = disable GRO/GSO/TSO on A2/A3 for night batch, rollback to vendor-fix later. Link to runbook?
Ash: Created temporary patch applied to 6 nodes in the pair via Ansible (playbook run id: pb-7812). Observed p95 drop back to ~8–12ms within 30s :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-135 (priority P2) — ticketing vendor + scheduling ToR inspection.
Greg: For next steps: 1) capture full NIC debug logs from the 6 nodes, 2) vendor bug report with TX_DMA_TIMEOUT examples, 3) test with smaller MTU at endpoints as a reproducible case.
Maya: I'll schedule a rollback window for the ToR microcode tomorrow if vendor asks us to revert. Also enabling continuous RDMA counter collection for the next 48h.
Dave: Temp mitigation cost: slightly higher CPU util on networking (GRO off), but token latency improved. Track cost delta in the console.
Lina: Thanks team — I'll draft a short postmortem template with timeline, root-candidate (GRO/GSO + ToR MTU mismatch + NIC DMA timeouts), and action items.
Ash: Will attach packet captures and the ib_write_bw logs to the ticket. Follow-up tomorrow AM for root-cause update.
Maya: thx — adding vendor contact @mellanox-supp to the ticket.
Ash: closing thread for tonight, will update if anything regresses.
